### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via datasources.external.draft (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/tables/:remote/draft, selected by route anchor /tables/:remote/draft), datasources.external.import (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/tables/:remote/import, selected by route anchor /tables/:remote/import), /tables/:remote/draft (route, bridged from symbol generateObjectDraft — its route source's handler names it), /tables/:remote/import (route, bridged from symbol importObject — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR (literal, a string literal in importObject; a string literal in notAFederationSourceError; a string literal in primaryDatasourceNotFederatedError))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 425c743fd9b80005d83e528dfdc8a5f8c68c8b30` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c646f942b89c5fb88062ba85657064c4f10773b1 && git checkout c646f942b89c5fb88062ba85657064c4f10773b1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 425c743fd9b80005d83e528dfdc8a5f8c68c8b30 658d9d0b54fb68201710b21904e6adf9e8b03159 && git checkout -B drift-repro 425c743fd9b80005d83e528dfdc8a5f8c68c8b30 && git merge --no-ff 658d9d0b54fb68201710b21904e6adf9e8b03159
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 425c743fd9b80005d83e528dfdc8a5f8c68c8b30` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `658d9d0b54fb68201710b21904e6adf9e8b03159`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/managed-datasource-sync-refusal.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/primary-datasource-test-and-sync.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/external-metadata-read-at-use.test.ts, packages/rest/src/remote-tables-twin.equivalence.test.ts + packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md

Inputs: card #24837 (body and comments `6331033735`, `6332488694`, `6332519276`, `6332527785`), PR #25167 (body, file list, the net diff of this head against `main`: 6 files, +550/-53), and the check-runs on this head. The five required contexts are `success` on this head (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`); `Check Changeset` and `Check PR Size` are `success`; the PR-run `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` (fast set; its shards skipped by path). Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The accept set of the six Sync doors, each read to its producer and its catch — right.** The one producer is `ExternalDatasourceService`; the new private `assertFederationSource(datasource, door)` is the first statement of `listRemoteTables`, `generateObjectDraft`, `importObject` and `refreshCatalog`. It refuses, in this order: `default` by name (`primaryDatasourceNotFederatedError`, unchanged text), then anything `isFederationSource(ds)` rejects, where `isFederationSource` is `Boolean(ds?.schemaMode) && ds?.schemaMode !== 'managed'` over `config.getDatasource(name)`. That rejects exactly three shapes: a declared `schemaMode: 'managed'`, a definition with no `schemaMode`, and no definition at all (`undefined`); with `SchemaModeSchema` closed to `managed | external | validate-only`, nothing else is refused. Codes and statuses per door, read in the cited code:

- admin `GET /datasources/:name/remote-tables` and `POST /datasources/:name/object-draft` (`admin-routes.ts`): the handler calls the service inside `try`, and `badRequest` answers `400` with `SERVICE_ERROR_CODE['external-datasource']` = `EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR` for every throw except a `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` relay (the guard throws `status: 400`, so the relay arm is not taken). Right.
- REST `GET …/external/tables`, `POST …/external/tables/:remote/draft`, `POST …/external/refresh-catalog` (`external-datasource-routes.ts`): the catch is `refused`, i.e. `answerThrown(res, err, 'EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR')`, which answers `400` with that literal code for any non-sandbox throw. Right.
- REST `POST …/external/tables/:remote/import`: the catch is `answerThrown(res, err, 'EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR')`, `400` with that code for every refusal — the code that door already served for `default`'s refusal and for every other refusal it relays. The guard's `door: 'import'` spells the same code at the throw, so the declaration and the served envelope agree. Right, and the card's literal "EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR for Sync's three routes" is correctly read as "the code each door already serves": no code is minted or moved, and `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` reads both literals (green in `Lint & Repo Gates`).
- A name with no definition answers `400`, not `404`: on these doors an unknown name already answered `400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR` (the introspector's "no driver introspection available" throw, through the same catch), so `400` is the existing answer and a `404` would have been a new code on the door. Right under the card's constraint.

**(b) `external` and `validate-only` keep every answer — right.** `isFederationSource` admits both. `listRemoteTables` reads the same definition it read before (now from the guard's return instead of `Promise.all`, a serialisation with no answer change) and keeps the `allowedSchemas` and unattributed-schema logic byte for byte; `generateObjectDraft` delegates to the private `draftObject`, which is the old body unchanged; `importObject` keeps its `persistObject`, name and prefix checks and now calls `draftObject` instead of re-entering `generateObjectDraft` (one judgment per request, under the import's own code); `refreshCatalog` is the old body after the guard. `testConnection` does not call the guard (Test is unchanged). The pins hold `lake` (`external`) and `mirror` (`validate-only`) at `200` list, `200` draft, an import that saves one object, and a refresh, over the real `ObjectQL`, connection service, driver factory, plugin wiring and Hono admin routes; the twin fixture now declares `schemaMode: 'external'` and its 10 cases compare both spellings on a federation source, which is what twin equivalence needs.

**(c) `default`'s existing refusal — unchanged.** The guard's first line is the `DEFAULT_DATASOURCE_NAME` check with the same helper and the same message; it still precedes any definition read. The door-kind parameter yields `EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR` on the import and `EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR` elsewhere, the two literals `main` passed in by hand. Pinned ("remote-tables on default answers as #24772 left it").

**(d) Decided before any introspection — right.** All four methods `await` the guard before `config.introspect`; `main`'s `listRemoteTables` ran `introspect` and `getDatasource` concurrently, so a refused datasource WAS introspected there, and is not now. The REST and admin handlers call nothing but the admission gate before the service. Pinned twice: `introspectSchema` spies on every managed driver and the primary one stay uncalled across all four doors, and `introspectDatasource` is uncalled for an undeclared name.

**(e) The seat's answer A (refuse a name with no definition) — consistent, a narrowing within ADR-0015, not a widening beyond it.** The spec default is `schemaMode: SchemaModeSchema.default('managed')` (`datasource.zod.ts`), so a definition without the key is managed; ADR-0015 §1 makes remote-ness a property the datasource DECLARES (`schemaMode !== 'managed'`), and §4.2 allows `object.external` only there — a name nothing declares has declared no such thing. `validateObject` on `main` already read `!ds` as "not federated, nothing to validate", so before this PR an import on such a name produced an object the sweep never checked and the §5.3 write gate (which exempts managed datasources) never gated; A closes that with the one predicate both now ask. The composition cost is the hypothetical one the dev named: a host whose live drivers have no `datasource` record in the `'metadata'` service. `plugin.ts` wires `getDatasource` to `metadata().get('datasource', n)` resolved per call, and the dev's federation dogfood (the booted showcase's code-declared `showcase_external`, 20 tests) and the full battery passed on `145e52859`, which is the evidence that the shipped composition does read code-declared datasources through that door. The reversed pin in `external-metadata-read-at-use` is the honest record of the change and keeps the validate half.

Public-surface changes implied by the diff, each named: the four REST doors' and two admin doors' accept set narrows on the three shapes above (right, the card's route B); `validateObject` / `validateDatasource` / `validateAll` semantics unchanged (`!ds || !ds.schemaMode || ds.schemaMode === 'managed'` is exactly `!isFederationSource(ds)`); no export, type, route, query parameter, status or code is added or removed; `packages/rest` source is untouched; `packages/spec`, `packages/objectql`, objectui and ADR-0015 are untouched, as the claim required.

### ② Semver level

Right. The changeset is `'@objectstack/service-datasource': patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on their own line-initial lines, a `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM / TO / Unchanged / fix-for-an-integrator lines, and the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; the PR body carries the same two declaration lines and the title carries `!`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the correct kind: no key, accepted value, default or meaning that an author writes moves (the datasource schema and the object schema are untouched; the authoring door for `object.external` on a managed datasource is deliberately not narrowed here, see ③). A non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, the closed card #25105's ruling A as the brief states it). `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head, and the dev reports the level axis and `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0 on the body.

The `(narrowing)` arm's full dogfood battery: run by the dev on `145e52859` (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 287 passed, 3 skipped; Tests 2395 passed, 18 skipped). This head is `145e52859` plus exactly one hunk: one line in `packages/rest/src/remote-tables-twin.equivalence.test.ts` (the fixture's `schemaMode: 'external' as const`). That file is a vitest file, not a build input (`packages/rest` publishes `dist` only; nothing outside it imports it), and the dogfood battery is `@objectstack/dogfood`'s own suite over a booted app, so none of the battery's inputs moved between `145e52859` and this head. The battery stands for this head. The PR-run `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head is `success` (the fast set, as PR runs carry); the full battery runs on `main` after landing.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Console still offers "Sync objects" on managed rows** (PR Acceptance notes; dev finding 1). Routed by the seat: an objectui card is filed when this PR lands (`6332519276`, item 1). Until then the button on a managed row opens the dialog with this refusal's message, which names the rule and the remedy, so the console is not silently broken. Not this PR's.
2. **ADR-0015 §4.2's "enforced at metadata-load time" has no enforcing site**: `defineStack` and the metadata save door accept `object.external` on a managed datasource (dev finding 2). Routed by the seat as #25168 for triage (spec or objectql lane). This PR closes the Sync producer of such objects only, and says so; retiring or amending the rule would be an ADR change this PR correctly does not take.
3. **No ADR anchor JSON for the guard** (`scripts/adr-anchors/`). Answered, not blocking: the ADR id is in the code and the refusal text, `check:adr-anchors` is green, and no anchor for ADR-0015 names this service today (the only anchor citing 0015 is `packages__objectql__src__search-companion.ts.json`), so the omission adds no drift. Escalated to the seat as a lane follow-up: anchor `assertFederationSource` under Prime Directive 13's corollary when the file surface is declared.
4. **REST-door refusal pins (draft, import, refresh on a managed datasource) measured once, not committed** (they belong in `packages/rest`, `domain:cli`). Answered, not blocking: the REST catches map every service throw to a fixed `400` code per door by construction (read above), and the service-level pins hold each method's code and status; the twin test pins the external list path at `200` on both spellings. Escalated to the seat: a `packages/rest` pin of the four doors refusing a managed datasource with their codes, alongside the twin file, when the lane declares it.
5. **The import door answers `EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR`**, and **refresh-catalog is refused too** (dev deviations, accepted by the seat in `6332519276`). Both right: see ①(a); the fourth method sits behind the same producer and `default`'s refusal already covered it.
6. **`origin/main` not merged before opening; first commit titled `wip(…)`**. `main` has moved by docs and spec-prose commits with no overlap with the touched packages; the PR is mergeable clean, and the queue rebuilds the merge. The squash landing takes the PR title. No action.
